title: MFO — R package for Maximal Fat Oxidation and kinetics
text: R package MFO (CRAN: v0.1.0, 2022; GitHub: v0.2.0, Feb 2026). Computes maximal fat oxidation (MFO), Fatmax, Fatmax zone, crossover point SIN kinetics model (Chenevière 2009) indirect-calorimetry data. Target users: sport health scientists. Roadmap: v0.2.x CRAN -> v0.3.0 (reliability, uncertainty, protocols, importers, Shiny app) -> JOSS paper. scientific specification lives docs/SPEC.md (exported project doc “MFO: fundamentos científicos y técnicos”). Sections 9.5 12–17 backlog. Read SPEC.md touching formula. Never change coefficient without citing source roxygen block adding unit test paper’s numbers.

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation and Kinetics Calculation
text: step contributes one point (FAT, %VO2max). method chooses maximum located: "P3" (default): third-degree polynomial FAT(x)=+bx+cx2+dx3\mathrm{FAT}(x) = + bx + cx^2 + dx^3, xx = %VO2max. Fatmax root b+2cx+3dx2=0b + 2cx + 3dx^2 = 0 lies within measured range gives highest FAT. Falls back P2 warning cubic fitted. "P2": parabola, Fatmax =−b/2c= -b / 2c. stable steps, forces symmetric curve. "MV" (measured values): step highest observed FAT (author equations). curve fitted: R_squared RMSE NA Fatmax zone uses linear interpolation steps. "MRER" (Chenevière et al., 2009): 1−RER=a1+b1x1 - \mathrm{RER} = a_1 + b_1x VO2=a2+b2x\mathrm{VO_2} = a_2 + b_2x fitted straight lines, FAT=1.7(1−RER)VO2\mathrm{FAT} = 1.7\,(1 - \mathrm{RER})\,\mathrm{VO_2} parabola Fatmax vertex, x=−(a1b2+a2b1)/(2b1b2)x = -(a_1b_2 + a_2b_1)/(2b_1b_2). Falls back MV warning vertex maximum inside measured range. v0.2.0 "MRER" returned highest observed step, now "MV". P3, P2 MRER fit’s R_squared RMSE returned. Fatmax zone range intensities fitted FAT ≥ 90 % MFO (Achten et al., 2002). crossover point intensity CHO exceeds FAT, linear interpolation steps.

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation and Kinetics Calculation
text: MFO_kinetics() normalises fat oxidation %MFO (highest observed step = 100 %) fits three-parameter sine model Chenevière et al. (2009, eq. 14) directly observed steps non-linear least squares (minpack.lm::nlsLM), prior smoothing: %MFO(x)=sin⁡{[π1/sπ+2d(Kx+d+t)]s},K=π100 \%\mathrm{MFO}(x) = \sin\left\{\left[\frac{\pi^{1/s}}{\pi + 2d}\left(Kx + d + t\right)\right]^{s}\right\}, \qquad K = \frac{\pi}{100} d (dilatation): d > 0 widens curve, d < 0 narrows . s (symmetry): s > 1 shifts peak right steeper fall; s < 1 opposite. t (translation): t > 0 shifts whole curve left. d = 0, s = 1 t = 0 curve half sine wave peaking 50 %VO2max. Fatmax Fatmin follow closed form equation: Fatmax = [(π + 2d)·2^(−1/s) − d − t]/K Fatmin, second zero curve, = (π + d − t)/K (fatmin_threshold gives threshold instead, e.g. 0.05 MFO). Chenevière et al. fitted exercise steps RER ≤ 1.0: RER_cutoff = 1 reproduces selection, include_basal = TRUE departs . SIN sensitive last step handled (negative_FAT); see ?MFO_kinetics.

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation & FatMax Function — MFO
text: step_time often data collected (seconds). db_MFO database containing MFO test. db_basal database containing basal test. db_graded database containing incremental exercise test (optional VO2max provided). VO2max highest mean VO2 `vo2max_window` seconds consecutive records. cv_var variable estimate coefficient variation. Can : "VO2", "VCO2" "RER". author author estimate MFO. Can : "Frayn", "Jeukendrup" "Peronnet". "Jeukendrup" warns exercise step outside 40-75 % VO2max, range Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5); resting row never warns. VO2max VO2max can passed directly (ml/min) instead using db_graded. given, `VO2max` used `db_graded` ignored warning. method method locate MFO Fatmax: "P3" (3rd-degree polynomial, default), "P2" (2nd-degree polynomial), "MV" (measured values) "MRER" (RER method). See section *Methods*. step_duration duration exercise step seconds (default 180 = 3 min). steady_state_duration duration steady-state period average within step, seconds (default 60). RER_cutoff RER value steps excluded (default NULL = cutoff), number name, following Amaro-Gahete et al. (2019, Front Physiol 10: 909, doi:10.3389/fphys.2019.00909 ): "classic" = 1.00 (Cheneviere et al. 2009 averaged steps RER <= 1.0); "safe" = 0.95, end--test RER recommend safe capture MFO; "sedentary" = 0.93 "trained" = 0.90, mean RER MFO report groups. Low cutoffs leave steps (SPEC 4, 19 finding 2). negative_FAT handle negative fat oxidation values: "truncate" (set 0, default), "exclude" (remove fitting), "keep" (include fitting). body_mass body mass kg (optional, relative MFO calculation). fat_free_mass fat-free mass kg (optional, FFM-relative MFO calculation). HRmax maximum heart rate bpm (optional, FatMax %HRmax). vo2max_window averaging window seconds VO2max `db_graded` (default 30). multiple `step_time`, number records rounded (30 s 20-s records uses 2 records = 40 s). See SPEC 9.5 14. include_basal logical. `TRUE`, resting row (`db_basal`) enters `MFO_db` step 0 part curve fit, Montes de Oca et al. (2021, Eur J Sport Sci, doi:10.1080/17461391.2020.1788650 ). Default `FALSE` fits exercise steps reproduces v0.1.0/v0.2.0, dropped resting row. `TRUE` P3/P2 fit changes; resting row `HR = NA` `Load = "basal"`. See SPEC 9.5. energy_equivalents kcal per g used `Kcal` `x_Kcal`: "classic" (4 kcal/g CHO, 9 kcal/g FAT, v0.2.0) "source" (values source `author`: Peronnet & Massicotte 1991 "Peronnet" , package decision, "Frayn"; Jeukendrup & Wallis 2005, Table 5, "Jeukendrup"). Default "classic" 0.2.x; change "source" 0.3.0, message says per session argument set. MFO Fatmax (g/min) depend . See [substrate_oxidation()] SPEC 19 (finding 1).

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation & FatMax Function — MFO

MFO_plot: ggplot object MFO plot including FAT CHO curves. MFO: Maximal fat oxidation (g/min). MFO_relative: MFO relative body mass (mg/kg/min), body_mass provided. MFO_FFM: MFO relative fat-free mass (mg/kgFFM/min), fat_free_mass provided. FAT_MAX: Intensity elicits MFO (% VO2max). FAT_MAX_HR: Heart rate FatMax (bpm), interpolated data. FAT_MAX_porcHRmax: FatMax % HRmax, HRmax provided. FatMax_zone_lower: Lower bound FatMax zone (% VO2max). FatMax_zone_upper: Upper bound FatMax zone (% VO2max). FatMax_zone_method: "fitted curve", "linear interpolation" `method = "MV"`. crossover_point: Intensity CHO > FAT (% VO2max). R_squared: R-squared fitted model (`NA` "MV"). RMSE: Root mean squared error fitted model (`NA` "MV"). method: Method used curve fitting. VO2max: VO2max used express intensity (ml/min). VO2max_window: effective averaging window VO2max (s); NA VO2max supplied. text: MFO_data data frame obtained MFO function (must contain FAT porc_VO2 columns). fatmin_threshold `NULL` (default) Fatmin second zero curve, proportion MFO (0, 1), e.g. 0.05, intensity Fatmax fat oxidation falls fraction MFO (closed form: \[(pi + 2d) ((pi - asin(threshold)) / pi)^(1/s) - d - t\] / K). v0.2.0 used fixed 5 % threshold searched grid.

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation Kinetics (SIN Model) — MFO_kinetics
text: Returns list contains: MFO_kinetics_data: `MFO_data` plus normalized %MFO (`porc_MFO`, 100 = highest observed FAT). MFO_kinetics_plot: ggplot object observed %MFO, basic SIN fitted SIN. d: dilatation parameter (width curve). t: translation parameter (horizontal shift along intensity axis). s: symmetry parameter (controls curve shape asymmetry; <1 left-skew, >1 right-skew). Fatmin: exercise intensity (% VO2max) second zero curve,   `fatmin_threshold` MFO given. FatMax_SIN: exercise intensity (% VO2max) peak fat oxidation SIN model. R_squared: R-squared SIN model fit (observed proportions MFO). RMSE: Root mean squared error SIN model fit (proportion MFO). d_se: standard error dilatation parameter. s_se: standard error symmetry parameter. t_se: standard error translation parameter. convergence: logical, whether SIN model converged.

(2009, Med Sci Sports Exerc 41: 1615-1625, p. 1618, doi:10.1249/MSS.0b013e31819e2f91 ): $$\%MFO = \sin\{[\pi^{1/s} / (\pi + 2d) \cdot (Kx + d + t)]^s\},       \quad K = \pi/100,$$ x % VO2max. v0.2.0 package computed (pi^(1/s)/pi) + 2d, `d` (`t`) comparable published values (SPEC 6.5, 19).

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation Kinetics (SIN Model) — MFO_kinetics
text: Cheneviere et al. (2009), model fitted non-linear least squares (Levenberg-Marquardt, [minpack.lm::nlsLM()], start d = 0, s = 1, t = 0) directly observed rows `MFO_data`, fat oxidation expressed proportion highest observed value (%MFO / 100). smoothing synthetic grid: v0.1.0/v0.2.0 fitted SIN fine grid predicted third-degree polynomial, inflated n shrank standard errors d, s t (SPEC 19, finding 7). R-squared RMSE computed observed proportions. least 4 rows needed 3 parameters: fewer function warns returns `convergence = FALSE`; 4 5 fits warns fit unreliable least 6 steps recommended (SPEC 6.5). `FatMax_SIN` `Fatmin` come closed forms derived eq. \[14\]: Fatmax = \[(pi + 2d) 2^(-1/s) - d - t\] / K , default, Fatmin = second zero curve = (pi + d - t) / K, Cheneviere's definition (SPEC 19, finding 3). Fatmin can lie beyond last observed step (extrapolation).

title: Substrate oxidation equations — substrate_oxidation
text: Rule: coefficient printed source used printed; derived coefficient used source prints equation (SPEC 19). **Frayn (1983)** (J Appl Physiol 55: 628-634, eqs. 5 6, n = 0), printed: CHO = 4.55 VCO2 - 3.21 VO2, FAT = 1.67 VO2 - 1.67 VCO2. Deriving Table 1 constants (glucose 0.746/0.746, fat 2.03/1.43 L/g) gives 4.535/3.195 1.667/1.667; cross-check tests. **Peronnet & Massicotte (1991)** (Can J Sport Sci 16: 23-29) print equations. package derives O2/CO2 constants Table 1 (glucose 0.7455/0.7426, fatty acid 2.0092/1.4136 L/g) solving VO2 = 0.7455 CHO + 2.0092 FAT VCO2 = 0.7426 CHO + 1.4136 FAT CHO FAT: CHO = 4.58519 VCO2 - 3.22597 VO2, FAT = 1.69469 VO2 - 1.70130 VCO2. v0.2.0 rounded 4.585 / 3.2255 / 1.6946 / 1.7012 used (SPEC 19, finding 6). **Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005)** (Int J Sports Med 26 Suppl 1: S28-S37), coefficients printed Table 5: 50 % VO2max (40-50 % set): CHO = 4.344 VCO2 - 3.061 VO2; 50 % VO2max (50-75 % set): CHO = 4.210 VCO2 - 2.962 VO2; FAT = 1.695 VO2 - 1.701 VCO2 . `phase = "rest"` printed equation: Jeukendrup & Wallis propose none. package decision (pure glucose, glycogen use rest), pair derived O2/CO2 constants Table 4 (glucose 0.7455/0.7426, fatty acid 2.0092/1.4136 L/g) solving 2x2 system: CHO = 4.58519 VCO2 - 3.22597 VO2, FAT = 1.69469 VO2 - 1.70130 VCO2. derivation 50/50 20/80 glucose/glycogen reproduces Table 5 coefficients within 0.005 kept cross-check tests. Table 5 sets defined 40-75 % VO2max . 40 % 40-50 % set 75 % 50-75 % set extrapolated; [calculate_vars()] warns exercise step falls outside range (SPEC 3, 9.5). Resting values (`phase = "rest"`) never trigger warning. **Energy equivalents** (`Kcal = CHO * e_cho + FAT * e_fat`, SPEC 19, finding 1): "classic": 4 kcal/g CHO 9 kcal/g FAT every equation (v0.2.0).   Default 0.2.x; default change "source" 0.3.0. "source", `author = "Peronnet"`: glucose 3.8683 fat 9.7460 kcal/g   (Peronnet & Massicotte 1991, Table 1). "source", `author = "Frayn"`: Frayn (1983, p. 632) gives energy   equivalents; package decision Peronnet & Massicotte values used. "source", `author = "Jeukendrup"`: Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5),   CHO 3.95 kcal/g 50 % VO2max (40-50 % set) 4.07 kcal/g   50 % (50-75 % set), fat 9.75 kcal/g. rest (`phase = "rest"`, pure glucose   pair, package decision) Peronnet & Massicotte glucose fat values used,   constants pair. `Kcal` jumps 50 % VO2max   CHO value.

title: MFO (development version)
text: SIN model: MFO_kinetics() now implements equation [14] Chenevière et al. (2009), pi^(1/s) / (pi + 2*d); v0.1.0/v0.2.0 computed pi^(1/s) / pi + 2*d. describe family curves, fitted curve can , d t take different values: old d Chenevière’s dilatation comparable published values. Fig. 5 parameters (d = 0.18, s = 1.52, t = 0.21) old formula put Fatmax 28.9 %VO2max instead 58.2 (SPEC 6.5, 19 finding 5). SIN fitting procedure: MFO_kinetics() now fits model directly observed steps (%MFO normalised highest observed step), Chenevière et al. (2009) . v0.1.0/v0.2.0 fitted grid ≥ 50 points predicted third-degree polynomial, inflated n shrank standard errors d, s t. FatMax_SIN Fatmin now come closed forms derived eq. [14], Fatmin second zero curve, (π + d − t)/K, instead first grid point 5 % MFO. Example data (Frayn): d 0.144 -> −0.385, s 0.935 -> 0.910, t −0.093 -> 0.355, FatMax_SIN 36.0 -> 36.2, Fatmin 76.0 -> 76.4 %VO2max, R² 0.997 -> 0.965 (now observed steps); standard errors grow 20–60 fold honest size. negative_FAT = "exclude" RER_cutoff = 1 (Chenevière’s step selection) example gives s = 0.54 Fatmin = 85.3 %VO2max: SIN sensitive last step, see ?MFO_kinetics (SPEC 6.5, 19 findings 3 7). MFO_kinetics() now distinguishes two warnings: fewer 4 steps SIN fitted (convergence = FALSE, ); 4 5 steps fitted warns fit unreliable least 6 steps recommended (SPEC 6.5). VO2max db_graded now highest rolling mean new vo2max_window argument (default 30 s) instead single highest record. window multiple step_time, number records rounded (30 s 20-s records = 2 records = 40 s) message reports effective window. Fatmax, Fatmax zone crossover point (%VO2max) increase ratio old/new VO2max; MFO (g/min) unchanged. example data VO2max drops 3442 3315 ml/min Fatmax moves 34.8 36.2 %VO2max. Use vo2max_window = step_time reproduce v0.2.0 (SPEC 9.5, 14). Resting substrate oxidation (x_CHO, x_FAT, x_Kcal) now uses author equations test; always used Frayn . Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005) propose resting equation: author = "Jeukendrup" package uses 100 % glucose pair derived Table 4 constants (CHO = 4.58519 VCO2 − 3.22597 VO2, FAT = 1.69469 VO2 − 1.70130 VCO2), documented package decision. MFO Fatmax affected resting row part fit. Example data "Peronnet": resting CHO 0.130 -> 0.134 g/min, FAT 0.0726 -> 0.0723 g/min (SPEC 9.5). author = "Jeukendrup", MFO() now warns exercise steps fall outside 40–75 %VO2max, range Jeukendrup & Wallis (2005, Table 5) equations, lists intensities; steps extrapolated silently . Steps removed RER_cutoff resting row never warn. Values unchanged (SPEC 3, 9.5). substrate_oxidation() longer fails vectors author = "Jeukendrup"; value picks equation. VO2max db_graded given, VO2max now used db_graded ignored warning (v0.2.0 silently used db_graded).

title: MFO 0.1.0
